q: In which year did the Easter Rising take place?
why: The Rising began on Easter Monday, 24 April 1916.

q: Who founded the Land League in 1879?
why: Davitt founded it in Mayo in 1879. Parnell became its president.

q: In which year did the potato blight first strike Ireland, starting the Great Famine?
why: Blight first appeared in 1845 and the crop failed again in the years after.

q: Who became the first President of Ireland in 1938?
why: Douglas Hyde, a founder of the Gaelic League, took office in June 1938.

q: In which year did Ireland join the European Economic Community?
why: Ireland joined on 1 January 1973, at the same time as the UK and Denmark.

q: Which battle in 1690 saw William of Orange defeat James II?
why: The Battle of the Boyne was fought in July 1690 and was a major Williamite victory.

q: Which society did Wolfe Tone help to found in 1791?
why: Tone helped found the Society of United Irishmen in Belfast in 1791 and later played a part in the 1798 Rebellion.

q: Which act came into force on 1 January 1801 and united the parliaments of Ireland and Britain?
why: The Act of Union abolished the Irish parliament and sent Irish MPs to Westminster.

q: Who led the campaign that won Catholic Emancipation in 1829?
why: O'Connell led the Catholic Association, and emancipation let Catholics sit in parliament.

q: In which year was the Anglo-Irish Treaty signed?
why: The Treaty was signed in London on 6 December 1921.

q: Which leader's government introduced the 1937 Constitution, Bunreacht na hÉireann?
why: De Valera's Fianna Fáil government drafted it, and it was approved by referendum in July 1937.

q: In which year did the Irish Free State come into being?
why: The Irish Free State was established on 6 December 1922.

q: Which leader founded the Home Rule Party in 1870 (originally the Home Government Association)?
why: Isaac Butt founded the movement for Irish self-government within the United Kingdom.

q: Who led the Irish Parliamentary Party from 1880 to 1891?
why: Parnell was known as the 'uncrowned king of Ireland'.

q: In which year was Gladstone's first Home Rule Bill defeated in the House of Commons?
why: The First Home Rule Bill was defeated in the House of Commons in 1886.

q: Which organisation was formed in 1913 to defend Home Rule?
why: The Irish Volunteers were founded in Dublin in November 1913.

q: Which organisation was set up in 1913 to oppose Home Rule?
why: The UVF was formed in January 1913 under Edward Carson and James Craig.

q: Who led the Irish Citizen Army?
why: Connolly founded the Irish Citizen Army to defend workers during the Lockout.

q: In what year did the Dublin Lockout take place?
why: Employers locked out workers who joined the ITGWU, led by Jim Larkin.

q: Who was the leader of the Irish Transport and General Workers' Union during the Lockout?
why: Larkin led the union against William Martin Murphy and other employers.

q: Where was the headquarters of the rebels during the 1916 Rising?
why: The GPO in Sackville (now O'Connell) Street was the headquarters.

q: Who read the Proclamation of the Irish Republic outside the GPO?
why: Pearse read the Proclamation on Easter Monday 1916.

q: Which rebel leader was spared execution after the Rising because he was born in America?
why: De Valera's life was spared, partly due to his American birth.

q: Which party won a majority of Irish seats in the 1918 general election?
why: Sinn Fein won 73 of 105 Irish seats in the 1918 general election.

q: Where did the first Dail meet in January 1919?
why: The first Dail met in the Mansion House on 21 January 1919.

q: What was the name of the police auxiliary force recruited in 1920 from ex-soldiers?
why: They were known for their khaki and dark green uniforms.

q: What happened on Bloody Sunday, 21 November 1920?
correct: British forces fired on the crowd at Croke Park
why: Fourteen people were killed at a Gaelic football match in Croke Park.

q: Who was the Director of Intelligence of the IRA during the War of Independence?
why: Collins built an effective intelligence network.

q: What did the Government of Ireland Act (1920) do?
correct: Divided Ireland into two parts, each with its own parliament
wrong: Gave all of Ireland full independence
United the parliaments of Britain and Ireland
why: It created Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland, which was the start of partition.

q: Who led the Irish delegation to negotiate the Anglo-Irish Treaty in London?
wrong: Eamon de Valera and Cathal Brugha
why: Griffith led the delegation, with Collins a key member.

q: What oath did the Treaty require members of the Dail to take?
correct: An oath of allegiance to the Crown
wrong: An oath to the Dail only
why: The oath was one of the issues that split Sinn Fein.

q: Which two sides fought the Civil War from 1922 to 1923?
wrong: The IRA and the British Army
why: The Free State forces fought anti-Treaty IRA forces.

q: Who was the Free State leader who died in an ambush in August 1922?
why: Collins was killed at Beal na Blath, County Cork.

q: Who became head of the Free State government after the deaths of Griffith and Collins?
why: Cosgrave led the government from 1922 to 1932.

q: Which party was founded by Eamon de Valera in 1926?
why: Fianna Fail came to power in 1932.

q: Which party was founded in 1933 from Cumann na nGaedheal and others?
why: Fine Gael was formed by the merger of Cumann na nGaedheal, the Centre Party and the Blueshirts.

q: What was the Economic War (1932-1938) between Ireland and Britain about?
why: De Valera withheld land annuities and Britain imposed tariffs.

q: What was the Anglo-Irish Trade Agreement of 1938 notable for?
wrong: Ireland joined the League of Nations
why: The Treaty Ports of Cobh, Berehaven and Lough Swilly were handed back.

q: What did Ireland call the Second World War period?
why: Ireland remained neutral in the Second World War.

q: Which city in Ireland was bombed by German aircraft on 31 May 1941?
why: German bombs hit the North Strand area of Dublin.

q: Who became Taoiseach in 1959 and began the policy of economic expansion?
why: Lemass presided over economic growth and the first Programme for Economic Expansion.

q: Which economist's report in 1958 outlined the plan for economic expansion?
why: T. K. Whitaker, Secretary of the Department of Finance, wrote 'Economic Development'.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Northern Ireland?
why: Craig, Lord Craigavon, led from 1921 to 1940.

q: What was the civil rights movement in Northern Ireland during the 1960s about?
correct: Equal rights for Catholics in votes, jobs and housing
why: The Northern Ireland Civil Rights Association was founded in 1967.

q: What happened on Bloody Sunday in Derry on 30 January 1972?
correct: British paratroopers shot civil rights marchers
why: Thirteen people were killed on the day and a fourteenth died later.

q: What was the Sunningdale Agreement of 1973 designed to do?
correct: Create a power-sharing executive in Northern Ireland
why: It collapsed in 1974 after a loyalist strike.

q: What was the Good Friday Agreement of 1998?
correct: A peace agreement for Northern Ireland
wrong: The Treaty ending the Civil War
why: It set up power-sharing and North-South bodies.

q: Who was the Irish Taoiseach when the Good Friday Agreement was signed?
why: Bertie Ahern was Taoiseach from 1997 to 2008.

q: Which Irish president was the first woman to hold the office?
why: Mary Robinson was elected in 1990.

q: Which treaty established the European Economic Community in 1957?
why: The Treaty of Rome was signed by the six founding states.

q: What did the Marshall Plan provide?
correct: American economic aid to rebuild Europe
wrong: A trade agreement between Europe and Asia
why: The plan gave about 13 billion dollars of aid from 1948.

q: What was the Cold War?
correct: A period of tension between the USA and the USSR without direct war
wrong: A war between Germany and France
why: The superpowers competed over ideology and influence from 1945 to 1991.

q: What was the Berlin Wall?
correct: A barrier built in 1961 dividing East and West Berlin
wrong: A wall built by the Romans
why: It stood until 1989.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
why: The wall fell on 9 November 1989.

q: Which crisis in October 1962 brought the US and USSR close to nuclear war?
why: Soviet missiles in Cuba triggered a US blockade.

q: Which US president was in office during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
why: Kennedy negotiated a settlement with Khrushchev.

q: What was the Berlin Airlift (1948-49)?
correct: Supplies flown into West Berlin during a Soviet blockade
why: Allied planes supplied West Berlin for nearly a year.

q: What was NATO, founded in 1949?
correct: A military alliance of Western countries
why: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was a collective defence alliance.

q: Which alliance did the USSR create in 1955 in response to NATO?
why: Eastern bloc countries joined the Warsaw Pact.

q: What did the Truman Doctrine (1947) promise?
correct: US support for countries resisting communism
why: Truman pledged to support free peoples resisting subjugation.

q: In which year did Ireland join the United Nations?
why: Ireland was admitted to the UN in December 1955.
